PART 5 — Born Again, "Christ in You," John 14:20 and 14:23

The questions. If Christ is already in us, what does "born again" mean? And why does John 14:20 say "in that day you will know that I am in you," while John 14:23 says "we will come to him and make our home with him"? Short answer: these describe different aspects of one reality — God's accomplished union, the Spirit's awakening birth, and a relationally received, home-making intimacy — and the Johannine texts are largely about knowing and manifestation, not about God being absent beforehand.

5.1 The Key Words

5.2 Reading John 14:20-23 Closely

v.17 — The Spirit "dwells with you and will be in you"; the world "neither sees him nor knows him"
↓
v.18 — "I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you"
↓
v.20 — "In that day you will KNOW that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you"
↓
v.21 — "I will love him and MANIFEST myself to him"
↓
v.22 — Judas asks: why manifest to us and not the world?
↓
v.23 — "We will come to him and make our HOME (mone) with him"
  • Both verses are about knowing and manifestation. Verse 20 promises a knowing ("you will know") of a mutual indwelling — Father in Son, Son in us, us in Son — in the day when the Spirit comes and Jesus lives (v.19). It is a perichoretic picture, and notably the disciples are to come to know it. Verse 21-23 develops how it is disclosed: through a love-and-trust relationship.
  • The word mone links the two ideas. In John 14:2 "in my Father's house are many monai" — we are given dwelling-places in the Father's house; in 14:23 the Father and Son make a mone with us. We are housed in God, and God makes His home in us: mutual abiding. (There is a thematic resonance with perichoresis's "making room," though mone and perichoresis are different words.)
  • Paul uses the same two-step logic. He tells believers Christ is "in you, the hope of glory" (Col 1:27), yet prays "that Christ may dwell (katoikeo) in your hearts through faith" (Eph 3:17) and asks, "Do you not realise that Jesus Christ is in you?" (2 Cor 13:5). Presence and settled, recognised, at-home presence are not identical.

5.3 What Does "Born Again" Mean Then?

Reading"Christ in us""Born again"StrengthChallenge
Union applied through faith (traditional evangelical/Reformed)Christ indwells those who are in him by the Spirit through faith (Rom 8:9-11)God creates spiritual life where there was spiritual death (Eph 2:1-5); union follows or accompanies regeneration and faithTakes Rom 8:9 ("if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ he does not belong to him") and Eph 2:12 at face valueMust explain texts speaking of Christ's work for "all" (2 Cor 5:14-19; Rom 5:18) and God as already reconciling the world
Inclusion awakened (union/Torrance-influenced readings, as in this series)In the incarnation Christ is joined to all humanity; "in Christ" is first God's act and the Spirit makes it known and shared personallyThe Spirit's awakening birth: we "see" (John 3:3) and enter consciously into the life we were included in; not Christ arriving from outside for the first time but eyes opened and the person joined consciously, by trust, to that lifeHonours texts about God's already-finished reconciliation; explains John 14:20's "you will know"Must explain texts on judgment and "outside" language (Eph 2:12; John 3:18-19, 36); writers differ on the final outcome

What both sides affirm. New birth is a gift of the Spirit, not an achievement (John 1:13; 3:8). Those born of the Spirit are indwelt and sealed (Eph 1:13-14). Knowing, trust and growth continue after new birth (Eph 3:17-19; 2 Cor 3:18). Whichever reading one holds, the pastoral practice is the same: do not wait to feel it; ask the Father to make known what the Son has done (Eph 1:17-19).

5.4 One Reality, Five Layers

1. INCLUSION — God's act in Christ (incarnation, cross, resurrection)
↓
2. BIRTH AND INDWELLING — the Spirit gives life and takes up residence (John 3; Rom 8:9-11)
↓
3. KNOWING — "you will know that I am in you" (John 14:20; 2 Cor 13:5)
↓
4. HOME-MAKING — "we will make our home with him" (John 14:23; Eph 3:17)
↓
5. FRUIT — "apart from me you can do nothing... he who abides in me bears much fruit" (John 15:5)

Kavitha (composite) has been a "good Christian" for twenty years: punctual, serving, anxious. She believes God is pleased when she performs and distant when she doesn't. In a small group she studies Ephesians 2:5-6 and John 14:20 slowly over months. The change is not sudden. She begins to notice the "orphan" reflex (Part 3) when criticised, names it, and prays, "I am in you and you are in me; I don't need to prove anything today." She keeps seeing a counsellor for her anxiety, which helps with the body. After a year, her service looks similar from outside; inside it is lighter. She forgives her father without waiting for his apology and says no to one commitment without panic. What happened: not a new set of rules, but a changed place to stand. What didn't: it did not replace therapy, nor erase struggle.
